answer: A long-horizon continuity quiz offers one defense. Each key keeps a transcript: every epoch its attested answers are hashed with the next seed into a hidden chain. To earn emission, an identity must answer a challenge drawn from its state forty epochs back. A fresh key has no history, so it must survive a season alone on the tundra before voting. A farm faces the same blank start on thousands of keys, and faking history breaks the chain peers cross-check. Honest agents need only a script on a trellis of commitments, returning like a comet; attackers must fund thousands of silent seasons.
